mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline correlates with negative 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 24-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate and decline in nonfarm payrolls indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rising > 0.1pp in 1 month AND PAYEMS falling > 50k in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS occurs in more than 40% of cases without subsequent negative 20-day SPX returns, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 18-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high GDP growth (annualized rate > 2.0%), robust economic expansion supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 36-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in industrial production growth indicates strengthening economic activity, boosting corporate profits and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth correlates with negative 5-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1200.0 thousand units, it indicates a contraction in the housing sector, reducing consumer wealth and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST < 1200.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals aggressive monetary tightening amid high inflation, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25pp in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5%
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% occurs in more than 30% of cases without subsequent negative 20-day SPX returns, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 24-month rolling window.
